title: Auction House Botting and Third-Party Tools are Out of Control

posts.cooked:
With combat addons crossing into the beyond, it’s time to restrict addons and third-party software/sites that analyze and automate the Auction House. This breaks the game for 99% of players as much as any combat addon does, if not more.

Selling anything on the AH (particularly reagents, potions, and high-volume items) has become next to impossible because of how strong third-party tools have gotten and how many people are straight-up botting with them. People are able to monitor their auctions and undercuts over multiple accounts and servers all at the same time, and automate buying, posting, cancelling, and reposting.

This is destroying the economy for anyone who doesn’t use these tools, and more and more players are turning to automation because trying to compete and sell things normally, even with tools like TSM (using it in the way it’s intended, aka not botting), is becoming virtually impossible.

Here’s an anecdote that represents pretty much all of my AH interactions in the last few months, but especially this past week:

I post two potions to the AH. Just two. I have extras and want to get rid of them.
In the time it takes me to refresh the page, the person with 3000 of the same potion for sale has cancelled theirs, undercut mine, and has relisted 1500 of their 3000.

That time elapsed is maybe 2 seconds.

[Edit: I didn’t explain this well. Bots are cancel scanning and reposting faster than should be possible. The same player will do it over and over within a second or two of my posts, meaning they are alerted to the new post and able to cancel and relist theirs almost instantly. I know it’s a bot because it’s the same seller, and manual cancel scanning and relisting cannot be done that fast.]

This has been bad for a while, but the addition of housing and the subsequent increased movement of old-world materials has made it 100x worse. Unless someone happens to buy what you posted the exact moment you post it, you will get undercut by a bot. Every time. They don’t even need to undercut the price anymore, because whoever posted last shows up first. So it’s just a cycle of post, scan, cancel, repost — all automated.

I want to be as transparent as possible here: I use TSM on my bank alt for ease of item grouping and auctioning. Yes, it is convenient and saves lots of time. But I’m not automating it. I’m one person, on one account, on one server, manually hitting post, refresh, cancel. And even with using TSM I’m falling way behind. So I can’t imagine how awful it is for someone who doesn’t use that tool at all.

The people running bots with multiple accounts over multiple servers to hoard hundreds of millions of gold so “number go up feel good” are ruining this for everyone else. And if you’re not one of those people, you should be pissed off, too.

If Blizzard is going to continue adding gold sinks to the game, it’s time to recognize that the economy is a mess and the average player isn’t sitting on a mountain of wealth. Gold sinks will not fix this problem; in fact it makes it worse. The people who do have tens of millions of gold and do nothing but automate the AH over dozens of servers and accounts are not spending it on gold sinks. Regular players are.

Restrict the API.

Edited to add: The existing API provides an overwhelming amount of data used by legit auction addons, but it also funnels data to third-party tools that allow things like real-time, multi-account, multi-realm monitoring for undercuts, automatic cancelling and relisting, sniping, and so on. None of this info is top secret or hard to find. The biggest barriers are technical know-how and being able to run multiple accounts.

I would like to see the API restricted so that basic AH addons like Actionator continue to work while in the game, but all of the data scraping going to third parties is no longer available. This would ideally only affect those external, third-party tools, and would not affect anyone using the AH in a legitimate way — manual scanning, posting, cancelling, and so on while online and on their characters.

This is not unreasonable and should not be controversial.
